view.mismatchLead: This link is configured as {configured}, but the connected peer reports {actual}.
view.mismatchHint: The token may have been entered in the other framework’s plugin. Sending and receiving still work, because BN handles both bridge types identically. Update one side so the names match.
view.emptyBots: The bridge is connected, but has no bots. Sign in to an account in the framework.
view.unlisted: {count} more bots are not shown; this table displays up to {limit} rows. They are still available when adding push connections.
view.noSession: No bridge is currently connected with this token.
view.setupPrefix: Enter both values in the plugin: BN address
view.setupSuffix: and the token above. An incorrect token returns 401; an unreachable address prevents connection. Neither attempt appears in this connection list.
view.noToken: No token has been set. Connection attempts return 401, which the plugin treats as a configuration error and does not retry. Generate a token and enter it with the BN address in the plugin.
view.pausedNoToken: Disabled, with no token set. Connection attempts return 401, so enabling this link alone will not restore it. Generate a token and enter it with the BN address in the plugin.
view.pausedHint: Disabled. Connection attempts with this token return 503. The bridge retries with backoff and reconnects when enabled.
view.addressNotePrefix: This address must be reachable from
view.addressNoteSuffix: when BN runs on a NAS.

$manifest.name: Bot framework bridge
$manifest.description: Use bots configured in koishi / AstrBot with BN. Enter the BN address and token in the plugin to connect.

links.label: Bridge links
links.description: Add a link here, then enter its token and BN address in the koishi / AstrBot plugin to connect.
links.removeWarning: The plugin will no longer connect, and connections using its bots will no longer send messages.

bridgeKind.label: Bridge type
bridgeKind.description: Only changes the label in the dashboard. Both bridge types use the same protocol.
